I've fixed it: `![x\"x](x)` with `-x smarty` now outputs `

`, the same as the unescaped version. Nothing is committed. **Cause:** Smarty adds `"` and `'` to the list of characters a backslash can escape. Each escaped character is held as a placeholder (`\x0234\x03`) until the very end. In attribute values like `alt`, the serializer saw only the placeholder, so it had nothing to escape. A late step (`UnescapePostprocessor`) then turned the placeholder back into a raw `"` inside the already-serialized attribute, which produced invalid HTML. **Fix** (`markdown/inlinepatterns.py`): `Pattern.unescape()` already prepares text for use in attributes. It now also turns those placeholders back into the real characters at that point, so the serializer escapes them like any other `"`. That one method covers image alt and title, link title and href, reference-style links and images, and autolinks. Text outside attributes is unaffected, and a plain `\"` in a paragraph still renders as `"`. **Tests:** - New `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_smarty.py` (8 cases): the exact case from the issue, plus escaped `"` in image title, link title and href, in plain text, and escaped `'` and `&` in alt text. - `tests/test_syntax/inline/test_images.py`: one test that an escaped character in alt text still works without any extensions. - Changelog entry added in `docs/change_log/release-3.4.md`, without an issue number since I don't know it. **Test results:** - The new tests and `tests/test_syntax/inline/` pass (92 passed). - Running the whole suite with pytest stops during collection on `test_md_in_html.py` (a `TestSuite` class pytest can't collect), and that happens without my change too. With `python -m unittest discover tests` it runs: 981 tests, 8 failures. - Those 8 are the same raw-HTML block tests that fail with my change removed, probably because of differences in Python 3.12's built-in HTML parser. None of them involve escapes. An escaped `"` inside an `attr_list` value (`{: title="x\"y" }`) doesn't parse as an attribute list at all once smarty is on; that is a separate parsing quirk that this fix doesn't touch.
